Maintenance knowledge, findable in plain language

A technician on the shop floor types what the machine is doing, in German or in English, and reads back an answer with the protocols it was taken from — each one citable and openable. When no protocol matches, the system says so and shows no sources at all.

Live at maintenance.smartsupply.com.de. Four demo accounts — operator, techniker, schichtleiter, admin — are printed on the sign-in page together with the password they share. The role decides what an answer contains.

Latest release · interface and corpus in German and English · all inference on EU infrastructure.

Project overview

What it is

A question-answering assistant for maintenance protocols. On machines that run fifteen to twenty years on PLC or SCADA, the error code on the display is often all the machine offers. A technician types it, or describes the fault in German or English, and gets an answer with the protocols it came from. When no protocol fits, the answer is labelled ungrounded and shows no sources. It is not a ticketing or CMMS system, and every document in it is synthetic. Overview · requirements

Where it comes from

The rules come from my maintenance work in US and German plants. An Operator and a Techniker get different answers to the same question: the Operator sees only actions they may perform and is told when to escalate (ADR-003). Only a Schichtleiter may add protocols; uploads go through moderation, and an answer citing an unapproved source marks it (ADR-006). Error codes are also matched literally, because five characters carry almost no meaning for a vector search (ADR-009).

How it was built

One Spring Boot application split into ingestion, query and web modules, an Angular client, PostgreSQL with pgvector and Keycloak for sign-in (arc42, ADR-001, ADR-004). Both languages share one embedding space, so a German question finds an English protocol without any translation step. All inference runs on EU infrastructure (ADR-002). A chat model challenged the design, an editor agent implemented it, and I reviewed every pull request before merging it (AI-USAGE.md).

Why that is verifiable

Each decision is a dated record with the alternatives it rejected. The retrieval thresholds were measured on a fixed question set against the real provider, not chosen (ADR-008). CI runs unit, integration and browser tests on every pull request and publishes the backend and frontend coverage reports and the API reference on this site; the live Swagger UI answers against the running deployment.

What you can see in two minutes

The live application (four demo roles, password on the sign-in page), the decision records, and the pull request record.
